title: Functional groups
examples: What is the difference between an alcohol and an ether?
How do I know if a molecule has a carbonyl group?
Can functional groups change the properties of a molecule?

explain.say: Today we are learning about functional groups in organic chemistry. A functional group is a specific arrangement of atoms. It determines the chemical reactions of the molecule.
We can recognise common groups like the hydroxyl group in alcohols. This group is represented by the minus oh symbol. It makes the compound an alcohol.
Another important group is the carbonyl group found in aldehydes and ketones. This group contains a carbon double-bonded to oxygen. It is written as a carbon double-bonded to oxygen.
Homologous series are groups of compounds with a general formula. They all have the same functional group. They also differ by a repeating unit of methylene groups.
Consider the alcohols in a homologous series. They all have the -OH group. Each successive member has one more carbon atom. This shows the pattern clearly.
In everyday life, soap molecules show this concept well. Soap molecules have a long hydrocarbon chain and a polar functional group. This allows them to clean grease.

faq.q: What is the difference between a functional group and a homologous series?
faq.a: A functional group is a specific group of atoms like -OH. A homologous series is a family of compounds that share that same functional group and follow a predictable pattern.
asks: Do I need both to describe a molecule?

faq.q: Does the functional group always determine the reaction?
faq.a: Yes, generally speaking, the functional group is the site where the chemical reaction will occur. It dictates the chemical behaviour of the entire molecule.
asks: Can the rest of the molecule stop the reaction?

faq.q: If I change the functional group, does the formula change?
faq.a: Yes, changing the functional group means you are changing the chemical nature of the molecule. This changes its properties significantly.
asks: Does the chemical name change too?

faq.q: What is the simplest example of a functional group?
faq.a: The hydroxyl group, -OH, is a very common and simple functional group found in alcohols. It is easy to spot when you learn to look for it.
asks: Which group is easiest to see?
Can you show me a simple example?

faq.q: What is the general formula for a homologous series?
faq.a: The general formula shows the pattern. For simple alkanes, it is C n H 2 n + 2. This formula helps predict the next member in the series.
asks: How do I write the pattern?
Is it always C n H 2 n + 2?

facts: Functional groups are specific arrangements of atoms within a molecule.
The presence of a functional group determines the chemical properties of the compound.
Homologous series are groups of compounds that share a common functional group.
Alcohols contain the hydroxyl functional group, which is represented as -OH.

quiz.say: Which group is responsible for the chemical reactions in an alcohol?
quiz.why: The hydroxyl group is the defining functional group for alcohols.

wrong.0: While the whole molecule reacts, the specific group dictates the type of reaction.
wrong.1: Hydrogen atoms are everywhere, but the functional group is the key feature.
wrong.3: The carbon chain is the backbone, but the functional group determines the reaction.

quiz.say: If a series increases by one methylene unit, what is this called?
quiz.why: This consistent pattern of adding a methylene unit defines a homologous series.

wrong.0: The general formula describes the pattern, but the series is the collection of compounds.
wrong.2: Isomers have the same formula but different structures, not necessarily a consistent series.
wrong.3: A functional group is a part, not the entire series concept.

quiz.say: A molecule with the structure C=O is likely to be a:
quiz.why: The C=O structure is the definition of the carbonyl group found in these classes.

wrong.1: Alkanes only have single bonds between carbons.
wrong.2: Alcohols must contain the -OH group, not just C=O.
wrong.3: Ethers contain an oxygen atom linking two carbon groups.
